Who is credited with discovering Big Bang?

Before he ever entered Parliament, this Welshman was a miners' union firebrand in the 1926 general strike — but he's best remembered for spearheading the creation of the British National Health Service as Attlee's Minister of Health. Who was he?

Aneurin Bevan (15 November 1897 - 6 July 1960) was a Welsh Labour Party politician, noted for spearheading the creation of the British National Health Service during his tenure as Minister of Health in Clement Attlee's government.

This Burmese politician and diplomat served as State Counsellor from 2016 to 2021 and was instrumental in Myanmar's transition from military rule toward democracy. She's been the general secretary of the National League for Democracy since the party's founding in 1988 — who is she?
Aung San Suu Kyi (born 19 June 1945) is a Burmese politician, diplomat and author who served as State Counsellor of Myanmar and Minister of Foreign Affairs from 2016 to 2021.
Once Lord Mayor of Dublin, this Fianna Fáil leader became the second-longest-serving Taoiseach before resigning in 2008 amid the Mahon Tribunal's revelations — who is he?
Bertie Ahern (born 12 September 1951) is an Irish former Fianna Fil politician who served as Taoiseach from 1997 to 2008, and as Leader of Fianna Fil from 1994 to 2008.

Born to a Syrian family and raised Muslim, this Argentine president converted to Catholicism to pursue politics and ran the country for a full decade under his namesake brand of Peronism — who was he?
Carlos Menem (Spanish; 2 July 1930 - 14 February 2021) was an Argentine politician who served as the president of Argentina for ten years, from 1989 to 1999.

Nominated by President George H. W. Bush in 1991 to succeed Thurgood Marshall, this associate justice of the U.S. Supreme Court is the second African American to serve on the bench and the second longest-serving justice in history. Who is he?
Clarence Thomas (born June 23, 1948) is an American lawyer and jurist who has served since 1991 as an associate justice of the Supreme Court of the United States.

Demon is an evil or malevolent supernatural entity.

Eleanor Roosevelt (October 11, 1884 - November 7, 1962) was an American political figure, diplomat, and activist.

Ferdinand Schörner (12 June 1892 - 2 July 1973) was a German military commander and convicted war criminal, who held the rank of Generalfeldmarschall (Field Marshal) in the Wehrmacht of Nazi Germany during World War II.
Which American politician, a convicted felon, served less than a year representing New York's 3rd district before being expelled from Congress in 2023?
George Santos (born July 22, 1988) is an American former politician and convicted felon.

Born to a farming family, this Indian politician served as chief minister of Karnataka before a roughly 11-month stint as prime minister of India in 1996-97, and has led his regional party since 1999. Who is he?
H. D. Deve Gowda (born 18 May 1933) is an Indian politician who served as the prime minister of India for nearly 11 months, from 1996 to 1997.
A leader of the army's 'Control Faction' in the 1930s, this officer became Japan's wartime prime minister in 1941; his rule was marked by widespread state violence — who is he?
Hideki Tojo (30 December 1884 - 23 December 1948) was a Japanese military officer and politician who served as Prime Minister of Japan from 1941 to 1944 during World War II.
Once rated Ukraine's second-richest man, this Ukrainian-born Israeli billionaire co-founded PrivatBank in 1992 and later served as a regional governor during the early war with Russia — who is he?
Ihor Kolomoyskyi (born 13 February 1963) is a Ukrainian-born Israeli billionaire businessman, once considered the leading oligarch in Ukraine.
Sent to take refuge on the Bass Rock as a boy after his escort was attacked, this youngest son of Robert III ruled the Scots from 1406 to 1437 — who was he?
James I of Scotland (late July 1394 - 21 February 1437) was King of Scots from 1406 to 1437.

Born in Centreville, Mississippi and educated at Vanderbilt, UVA Law, and Oxford, this Republican has served as Louisiana's junior U.S. Senator since 2017 after 17 years as the state's Treasurer — name this politician?
John Kennedy (Louisiana politician) (born November 21, 1951) is an American politician and attorney who has served as the junior United States senator from Louisiana since 2017.
A WWI U-boat commander taken prisoner by the British in 1918, he later briefly became Nazi Germany's head of state after Hitler's suicide — who is it?

Karl Dönitz (16 September 1891 - 24 December 1980) was a German naval officer and politician who briefly succeeded Adolf Hitler as the head of state of Nazi Germany after the latter's suicide during the World War II in April 1945.
Widow of warlord Toyotomi Hideyoshi, this Buddhist nun founded a temple in Kyoto and monitored daimyo families held hostage at Osaka Castle — who was she?
Kōdai-in (died October 17, 1624), formerly known as Nene, One, Nei, was an aristocrat and Buddhist nun, founder of the temple Kdai-ji in Kyoto, Japan.
A Spanish Navy officer who fought in the Rif War and Civil War before rising through Franco's government, he was handpicked as the dictator's successor as head of government — who is he?
Luis Carrero Blanco (Spanish; 4 March 1904 - 20 December 1973) was a Spanish Navy officer and politician.
This retired U.S. Army general served as the 20th chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff from 2019 to 2023, after earlier serving as the Army's 39th chief of staff — who is he?
Mark Milley (born 20 June 1958) is a retired United States Army general who served as the 20th chairman of the Joint Chiefs of Staff from 2019 to 2023.
She served as deputy First Minister of Northern Ireland from 2020 to 2022 before rising to First Minister in 2024 — who is she?
Michelle O'Neill (ne Doris; born 10 January 1977) is an Irish politician who has been First Minister of Northern Ireland since February 2024 and Vice President of Sinn Fin since 2018.
This former footballer and journalist represented the Heingang constituency and rose to become Manipur's 12th Chief Minister, serving from 2017 to 2025 — who is he?

N. Biren Singh (Meitei; born 1 January 1961) is an Indian politician, former footballer and journalist who served as the 12th Chief Minister of Manipur from 2017 to 2025 as a member of the Bharatiya Janata Party.
This Indian politician has served as Minister of Road Transport & Highways since 2014, becoming the only person to hold that single portfolio for three consecutive terms — who is he?
Nitin Gadkari (born 27 May 1957) is an Indian politician who is serving as the 40th Minister of Road Transport & Highways since 2014.
Also known for the character Professor Kranz, this Italian actor and writer penned satirical books and became famous for grotesque comic creations, including a meek accountant — who is he?
Paolo Villaggio (30 December 1932 - 3 July 2017) was an Italian actor, comedian, film director, and writer.
Whether offered alone or in groups, as part of a set ritual or spontaneously, this act of communication with a deity can seek intercession, give thanks, or offer praise — what is it called?

After leading the Congress to victory in the 2023 state election that toppled the incumbent Bharat Rashtra Samithi, which politician became the current Chief Minister of Telangana?

Born in London to a Pakistani family and once a practicing solicitor, this Labour politician represented Tooting in Parliament before becoming the city's mayor in 2016 — who is he?
Sadiq Khan (born 8 October 1970) is a British politician serving as the third and current strategic authority mayor for London since 2016.
Known by the honorific 'Bangabandhu,' this Bengali politician led his country to independence and served as its founding president before being assassinated in a 1975 coup — who is he?

Sheikh Mujibur Rahman (17 March 1920 - 15 August 1975), also known as Mujib or by the honorific Bangabandhu, was a Bangladeshi politician, revolutionary, statesman, activist and diarist who was the founding president of Bangladesh.

This Russian right-wing populist politician led a nationalist party from its 1992 founding until his death in 2022, twice serving as deputy chairman of the State Duma. Who is he?

Vladimir Zhirinovsky (25 April 1946 - 6 April 2022) was a Russian right-wing populist politician who served as the leader of the Liberal Democratic Party of Russia (LDPR) from its creation in 1992 until his death in 2022.

Clarence Darrow: American lawyer and politician (1857–1938)
Rising from Persis to topple the Median Empire, this ruler founded the Achaemenid dynasty and built what became, in its day, the largest empire the world had yet seen — who was he?
Cyrus the Great: Founder of the Achaemenid Empire. Cyrus II of Persia (c. 600 – 530 BC), commonly known as Cyrus the Great, was the founder of the Achaemenid Empire.

On 11 March 2011 a major nuclear accident started at the Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant in Ōkuma, Fukushima, Japan. The direct cause was the Tōhoku earthquake and tsunami.

Germanwings Flight 9525: 2015 deliberate aircraft crash in France.

Harry S. Truman: President of the United States from 1945 to 1953.

Herzi Halevi: Chief of General Staff of the Israeli Defense Forces (born 1967)

Ion Antonescu: Dictator of Romania from 1940 to 1944.

July Revolution: 1830 overthrow of the Bourbon monarchy in France.
As chairman of a football ownership group, this Emirati executive oversees Manchester City and other clubs worldwide, while also serving as Abu Dhabi's Presidential Special Envoy to China. Who is he?
Khaldoon Al Mubarak: Emirati investment manager.

Luis Carlos Galán: Colombian politician (1943–1989). While the investigation into his assassination remains unsolved, Galan's assassination was a crucial factor in the downfall of the Medellin Cartel a few years later.
Sanskrit for 'circle,' this geometric configuration of symbols is used across Hindu, Buddhist, Jain, and Shinto traditions to aid meditation and represent sacred space — what is it?
Mandala: Spiritual and ritual symbol in Hinduism, Jainism and Buddhism.
Famed for slicing his military cloak in two with his sword to clothe a freezing beggar, this Roman-cavalry-veteran-turned-bishop became one of Europe's most venerated patron saints — who was he?
Martin of Tours: Christian cleric and saint (316/336–397)
Originating in Judaism, this Hebrew term for an anointed savior figure describes a future human leader descended from King David who will reunite the tribes of Israel — what is the title?
Messiah: Saviour or liberator of a group of people.
Killed during Hernán Cortés's seizure of Tenochtitlan, this ninth Aztec emperor presided over the empire at its largest territorial extent — who was he?
Moctezuma II: Tlahtoāni of the Aztec Empire until 1520.

Mustafa I: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire (r. 1617–1618, 1622–1623)
A Florentine diplomat of the Italian Renaissance, this man wrote a famous political treatise published only after his death and is often called the father of modern political science — who was he?

Turkish politician who rose from Istanbul mayor to prime minister (2003–2014) and has been president since 2014, co-founding the AKP. His rule has drawn criticism for democratic backsliding. Who is he?
Recep Tayyip Erdoğan: President of Turkey since 2014. Recep Tayyip Erdoğan (born 26 February 1954) is a Turkish politician and statesman who has been the president of Turkey since 2014.

Saint Valentine's Day Massacre: 1929 gang shooting in Chicago. The Saint Valentine's Day Massacre was the murder of seven members and associates of Chicago's North Side Gang on Saint Valentine's Day 1929.

Central to Judaism and recounted every Passover, this founding narrative describes the Israelites' escape from Egyptian bondage through a parting of the Red Sea under Moses — what is it?
The Exodus: Founding myth of the Jewish people.
According to Herodotus, this 6th-century BC queen of the Massagetae defeated and killed Cyrus the Great in battle — who was she?
Tomyris: 6th-century BC queen of the Massagetae. Tomyris became a popular subject in European art and literature during the Renaissance.

Wallis Simpson: Wife of Prince Edward, Duke of Windsor (1896–1986)

He started as a wildly successful Scottish privateer, commissioned by the governor of New York to hunt pirates and French ships in the Indian Ocean from his ship Adventure Galley — which sea captain, hanged in 1701, is it?
William Kidd: Scottish privateer (1654–1701). William Kidd (c. 1645 – 23 May 1701), also known as Captain William Kidd or simply Captain Kidd, was a Scottish privateer.
Claiming to be Catherine the Great's dead husband Tsar Peter III, this Cossack leader proclaimed an end to serfdom in 1773 and led a massive peasant uprising across the Volga-Ural region. Who was he?
Yemelyan Pugachev: Russian Cossack rebel leader (1742–1775)
A dispute between two rival lords escalated into a decade-long Japanese civil war from 1467 to 1477 that triggered the Warring States period — what was this conflict called?
Ōnin War: 15th-century civil war in Japan.
Who among these was born first?
Soichiro Honda (born 1906) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four was born earliest?
Henry Vaughan (born 1621) is the earliest of the four. Henry Vaughan (1621 – 23 April 1695) was a Welsh metaphysical poet, author and translator writing in English, and a medical physician.
Which of these four began earliest?
Messerschmitt Bf 109 (founded 1937) is the earliest of the four.
Which one below was established earliest?
C (programming language) (founded 1972) is the earliest of the four. C is a general-purpose programming language created in the 1970s by Dennis Ritchie.
Which one below is best known as a physicist?
Max Born is a physicist. During World War I, Born was originally placed as a radio operator, but his specialist knowledge led to his being moved to research duties on sound ranging.
Pick the chemist from these four.
Antoine Lavoisier is a chemist. It is generally accepted that Lavoisier's great accomplishments in chemistry stem largely from his changing the science from a qualitative to a quantitative one.
What is the atomic number of Oxygen?
Oxygen is a chemical element; it has the symbol O and its atomic number is 8.
In what year was Werner Heisenberg born?
Werner Heisenberg: Heisenberg published his Umdeutung paper in 1925, a major reinterpretation of old quantum theory.
In what year was Glutathione discovered?
Glutathione (GSH,) is a tripeptide made of the amino acids glutamate, cysteine, and glycine.
In what year was Morphine discovered?
Morphine, formerly known as morphium, is an opiate found naturally in opium, a dark brown resin produced by drying the latex of opium poppies (Papaver somniferum).
Acetylcysteine: Pfizer. It has been used to treat lactobezoar in infants.
In which country is Embraer E-Jet family based?
Embraer E-Jet family: Brazil. The E-Jet was designed to complement Embraer's earlier ERJ family, the company's first jet-powered regional aircraft.
Who is credited with discovering Radon?
Radon: Friedrich Ernst Dorn. Radon is a chemical element; it has symbol Rn and atomic number 86.
Who is credited with discovering Tautavel Man?
Tautavel Man: Henry de Lumley. Tautavel Man refers to the archaic humans which—from approximately 550,000 to 400,000 years ago—inhabited the Caune de l’Arago, a limestone cave in Tautavel, France.
Who is credited with discovering MDMA?
MDMA: Anton Köllisch. MDMA was first synthesized in 1912 by Merck chemist Anton Köllisch.
Though the word is often dropped from its name, invasive ductal carcinoma — the most common breast cancer — technically falls under this broader glandular cancer classification — what is it?
De Havilland Canada DHC-6 Twin Otter
Adenocarcinoma (AC) is a type of cancer made of cells from glands.
Formed naturally around volcanic vents and on burning coal dumps, this soluble white crystalline salt serves as both a fertilizer and a food additive — what's the compound with formula NH4Cl?
Ammonium chloride is an inorganic chemical compound with the chemical formula NH4Cl, also written as Cl.

This superfamily of tailless Old World primates, native to sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia and more closely related to Old World monkeys than New World ones, includes humans among its members — what's this group called?
Ape (hominoids), are a superfamily of Old World simians native to sub-Saharan Africa and Southeast Asia.
Found throughout North America from Canada to northern Mexico, this sea eagle has two subspecies and forms a pair with the white-tailed eagle—name it.
Bald eagle (Haliaeetus leucocephalus) is a bird of prey found in North America.

Found mainly in New Guinea, which family of forty-four species — the males famous for extravagant, elaborate plumage sprouting from their beaks, wings, tails, or heads — is confined largely to dense rainforest?
Bird-of-paradise are members of the family Paradisaeidae of the order Passeriformes.
This cabbage-family vegetable, whose large dark-green flowering head is eaten as food, closely resembles its paler relative cauliflower — name it?
Native to nearly all of South America, this semiaquatic, grass-munching cousin of the guinea pig holds the title of largest living rodent — what is it?
Capybara (Hydrochoerus hydrochaeris) is the largest living rodent, native to all countries in South America except Chile.

The smallest recognized dog breed in the world, this Mexican toy breed has large erect ears and a rounded skull, and its genes carry a trace of pre-Columbian indigenous American dog ancestry — which breed?

Chihuahua (dog breed) is a Mexican breed of toy dog and the smallest recognized dog breed in the world. It is primarily kept as a companion animal and is characterized by its compact size, large erect ears, and rounded skull.
This digestive condition refers to swelling or inflammation of the large intestine, and can be acute and short-lived or a long-term, chronic issue — what is it called?
Colitis is swelling or inflammation of the large intestine (colon). It broadly fits into the category of digestive diseases.
Together with birds, this order of predatory reptiles is one of only two survivors of the ancient Archosauria — and it lumps together alligators, caimans, and gharials. What is it?
Crocodilia is an order of semiaquatic, predatory reptiles that are known as crocodilians.
A colorless liquid that's a workhorse solvent for chemical reactions, this compound is officially odorless — yet degraded samples reek of fish thanks to a dimethylamine impurity; what is it?
Dimethylformamide is an organic compound with the chemical formula HCON(CH3)2.

This scientific and engineering discipline uses transistors, diodes, and integrated circuits to control and amplify the flow of electric current, converting between forms like AC to DC. What is the field called?

Electronics is a scientific and engineering discipline that studies and applies the principles of physics to design, create, and operate devices that manipulate electrons and other electrically charged particles.
They're a tiny minority by headcount among living things, yet their larger bodies make their combined biomass dwarf that of bacteria and archaea — what membrane-bound-nucleus group is this?
Eukaryote are the domain Eukaryota or Eukarya, organisms whose cells have a membrane-bound nucleus.
Systematically named methanal and carrying the formula CH2O, this pungent gas turns up in particle board, disinfectants, and lab specimen jars — what is it?

Formaldehyde (for-, US also fr-) (systematic name methanal) is a pungent colorless gas mainly used in the production of industrial resins, such as for particle board, coatings, plastics, pulp, paper, synthetic fibers, and textiles.
The tallest living land animal and the largest ruminant on Earth, this African mammal's closest living relative is the shorter-necked okapi — name the animal?
Giraffe (genus Giraffa) are large African hoofed mammals.
Named for a flattened, laterally extended head shape called a cephalofoil, with eyes placed at each end of the T, this family of sharks includes species mostly grouped in one genus — which sharks?

Hammerhead shark are a group of sharks that form the family Sphyrnidae, named for the unusual and distinctive form of their heads, which are flattened and laterally extended into a cephalofoil (a T-shape or "hammer").
This perennial root vegetable, a relative of mustard, wasabi, broccoli, and cabbage, is grated and used worldwide as a pungent spice and condiment — what plant is it?
This contagious bacterial skin infection most often shows up as yellowish crusts on a child's face, arms, or legs, and spreads easily in crowded day cares and contact sports — what is it?
Impetigo is a contagious bacterial infection that involves the superficial skin.
Director of Columbia's Center for Sustainable Development, which economist led the United Nations Millennium Project's work on the Millennium Development Goals?
Jeffrey Sachs (SAKS; born November 5, 1954) is an American economist and public policy analyst.
Native to Central and South American rainforests, this frugivorous nocturnal mammal related to raccoons and coatis shares its 'honey bear' nickname with an unrelated species — which animal?
Kinkajou (/kkdu/; Potos flavus) is a mammal of the family Procyonidae, a relative to olingos, coatis, raccoons, and the ringtail and cacomistle.
An indoor watchdog by tradition, this dog breed originated high in Tibet — which non-sporting breed is it?
Lhasa Apso is a non-sporting dog breed originating in Tibet.
Caused by a compromised lymphatic system, this condition raises infection risk in affected tissue and is treated with compression and massage rather than water pills — what is it?
Lymphedema (USA), lymphoedema (UK) also known as lymphatic edema (US)/oedema (UK), is a condition of localized swelling caused by a compromised lymphatic system.
This German-British theoretical physicist won a Nobel Prize for his statistical interpretation of the wavefunction, a cornerstone of quantum mechanics. Who is he?
Max Born (11 December 1882 - 5 January 1970) was a German-British theoretical physicist who was instrumental in the development of quantum mechanics.
This unit of time, normally equal to 60 seconds, can rarely stretch to 61 seconds under the UTC time standard because of a leap second — what is it?
Minute (symbol: min) is a unit of time defined as equal to 60 seconds.
Found from Africa to Southeast Asia, this snake genus contains the 'true cobras' as opposed to look-alikes like the king cobra — which genus?
Naja is a genus of venomous elapid snakes commonly known as cobras (or "true cobras").
What's the name for the scholarly study and collection of coins, paper money, tokens and medals — though by its rules, cigarettes traded in prison don't count?
Numismatics is the study or collection of currency, including coins, tokens, paper money, medals, and related objects.
Inflammation of the enzyme-and-hormone-producing organ behind the stomach, it comes in acute and chronic forms and can lead to diabetes — what is this condition?
Pancreatitis is a condition characterized by inflammation of the pancreas.
This Belgian-British microbiologist helped discover the Ebola virus in 1976 and led the fight against that first recorded outbreak before becoming a pioneering AIDS researcher — who is he?
Peter Piot (born 17 February 1949) is a Belgian-British microbiologist known for his research into Ebola and AIDS.

There are only five of these convex, regular three-dimensional shapes — including the cube, tetrahedron, and icosahedron — where every face is an identical regular polygon. What are these shapes called?
Platonic solid is a convex, regular polyhedron in three-dimensional Euclidean space.
Discovered in 1915 and too faint to see with the naked eye, which small, dim star, orbiting its two brighter neighbors once every 550,000 years, is our closest stellar neighbor after the Sun?
Proxima Centauri is the nearest star to Earth after the Sun, located 4.25 light-years (1.3 parsecs) away in the southern constellation of Centaurus.
Physicists denote this stretching of light's wavelength — caused by relative motion, gravity, or cosmic expansion — with the symbol z; its opposite is called blueshift. What is it?
Redshift is an increase in the wavelength, or equivalently, a decrease in the frequency, of electromagnetic radiation (such as light).

Grown mainly from Eastern and Northern Europe into Russia, this cold-tolerant grain crop is a member of the wheat tribe and its vigorous growth suppresses weeds while providing early forage for animals — name it?
Rye (Secale cereale) is a grass grown extensively as a grain, a cover crop and a forage crop.
This Russian politician has served as mayor of Moscow since 2010, after earlier stints as a regional governor, head of the presidential administration, and deputy prime minister — who is he?
Sergey Sobyanin (born 21 June 1958) is a Russian politician, serving as the 3rd mayor of Moscow since 21 October 2010.
Known by such nicknames as 'sour dock' and 'spinach dock,' this tangy Eurasian herb thrives wild in grasslands and is often used as a leaf vegetable — which plant?
Sorrel (Rumex acetosa) is a perennial herbaceous plant in the family Polygonaceae.
The fifth most common element on Earth, this multivalent nonmetal usually turns up in sulfide and sulfate minerals and is a bright yellow crystalline solid — what is it?
Sulfur (American spelling or sulphur (Commonwealth spelling) is a chemical element; it has symbol S and atomic number 16.

Proposed by Albert Einstein in special and general forms published in 1905 and 1915, this framework superseded 200-year-old Newtonian mechanics and explains gravitation's relation to the other forces of nature — name it?
Theory of relativity comprises two physics theories by Albert Einstein: special relativity and general relativity. Special relativity applies to all physical phenomena in the absence of gravity.

Native only to New Zealand and resembling a lizard, this reptile is the sole surviving member of an order that was hugely diverse in the Mesozoic era, with fossils dating to the Middle Triassic — what's the animal?
Tuatara (Mori:; Sphenodon punctatus) is a species of reptile endemic to New Zealand.
This Russian-American inventor built a television system using cathode-ray tubes and worked on image tubes and the electron microscope — who was he?
Vladimir K. Zworykin (1888/1889 - July 29, 1982) was a Russian-American inventor, engineer, and pioneer of television technology.

Native to freshwater and brackish habitats across western Eurasia, this ray-finned fish in the perch family, related to perch, ruffe, and darters, has become a popular game species well beyond its original range. Name it?
Zander (Sander lucioperca), sander or pikeperch, is a species of ray-finned fish from the family Percidae (which also includes perch, ruffe and darter).
Prescribed for ADHD and narcolepsy but also misused as a euphoriant, this fixed-dose pill packs four different amphetamine salts into one tablet. What is its brand name?
Adderall: Drug mixture used mainly to treat ADHD and narcolepsy.
This Scottish physician shared the 1945 Nobel Prize for discovering penicillin, and in 1922 identified an enzyme in his own nasal discharge — who is he?
Alexander Fleming: Scottish physician and microbiologist (1881–1955)
This inorganic salt, most commonly used as a soil fertilizer, is 21% nitrogen and 24% sulfur by content — what is it?
Known by the symbol Sb and mined chiefly from stibnite ore, which element has long been powdered into the cosmetic kohl and today hardens lead in car batteries?
Antimony: Chemical element with atomic number 51 (Sb)
His namesake effect — scattered X-rays losing energy — proved light behaves as particles and earned a share of the 1927 Nobel Prize in Physics. Who was this American physicist?

Flown by the Royal Air Force's Red Arrows display team, this British jet-powered advanced trainer has been license-built in India by Hindustan Aeronautics, with over 1,000 sold to 18 countries — which aircraft?
BAE Systems Hawk: Military training aircraft family.
Strawberries, blueberries, blackberries, and currants all fall under this small, pulpy, often brightly colored category of fruit — which Britain calls "soft fruit." What is it?
Berry: In the culinary sense, small edible fruit.
Announced in 2011, this fourth-generation narrow-body jet introduced more efficient LEAP engines and split-tip winglets, with variants from the 7 up through the 10 — what aircraft is it?
This volatile red-brown liquid element, with properties between chlorine and iodine, gets its name from the Greek word for 'stench' — which element?
Bromine: Chemical element with atomic number 35 (Br)
Designated Maryland's official state crustacean, this species is expected to benefit from climate change even as overfishing hurts other Chesapeake Bay fisheries — which species?
Callinectes sapidus: Species of crustacean. It is Maryland's largest commercial fishery and has been designated its state crustacean.
This corvid, native to western Europe and the eastern Palearctic, is stockier and larger than its North American cousin but nearly identical in appearance — what bird is it?
Carrion crow: Species of bird. The carrion crow (Corvus corone) is a passerine bird of the family Corvidae, native to western Europe and the eastern Palearctic.
Often called 'the father of the computer,' this English polymath designed the difference engine and the analytical engine, borrowing a punch-card principle from the Jacquard loom — who is he?
Charles Babbage: English mathematician, philosopher, and engineer (1791–1871)
One of the original citrus fruits, this large fragrant relative of the lemon has a thick, coarse rind and is a genetic ancestor of most modern citrus hybrids — what is it?

A member of the true thrushes, this Eurasian songbird whose nominate male is all black breeds across Europe, western Asia, and North Africa and has been introduced to Australia and New Zealand — which bird is it?
Common blackbird: Thrush native to Europe, western Asia and North Africa.
Also nicknamed the prairie wolf, this adaptable North American canine fills a similar ecological niche to Eurasia's golden jackal and was first spotted in Panama in 2013 — what is it?
Coyote: Species of canine native to North America.

Affecting about half of all adults and often treated with antifungal cream, this common scalp condition causes flaking and mild itchiness but isn't actually caused by poor hygiene. What condition is it?
Dandruff: Skin condition of the scalp. It can result in social or self-esteem problems.

Driven by a gradient in chemical potential, this stochastic process describes the net movement of particles from areas of higher to lower concentration and can even reverse direction in spinodal decomposition — what physical process is this?
Diffusion: Transport of dissolved species from the highest to the lowest concentration region.
Defined in humans as an adult height of four foot ten or shorter, this condition's most common form — accounting for about 70% of cases — is a genetic disorder called achondroplasia. What is it?
Dwarfism: Small size of an organism, caused by growth deficiency or genetic mutations.
This stage of development begins right after fertilization, progressing from a single-celled zygote through a ball of cells called a morula — what is it called?
Embryo: Multicellular diploid eukaryote in its earliest stage of development.
This white solid is prized for binding iron and calcium ions into water-soluble complexes — handy for dissolving scale — and goes by a four-letter acronym. What is it?
In this common vision condition, distant objects appear sharp but close-up objects blur because light focuses behind the retina instead of on it - what is it?
Farsightedness: Eye condition in which light is focused behind instead of on the retina.
Sold under the brand name Luvox, this SSRI antidepressant treats OCD and other anxiety disorders, with milder side effects than most in its class except gastrointestinal ones — what drug is it?
Fluvoxamine: SSRI antidepressant. Fluvoxamine, sold under the brand name Luvox among others, is an antidepressant of the selective serotonin reuptake inhibitor (SSRI) class.
Capable of living up to 177 years and weighing as much as 417 kilograms, which giant reptile — native to a chain of Pacific islands named for it — is the largest cold-blooded land animal alive today?
Galápagos tortoise: Species of reptile. The species comprises 15 subspecies (12 extant and 3 extinct).
Named from a Latin word for sword, this genus of cormous flowering plants in the iris family is sometimes called the 'sword lily' and is most diverse in South Africa's Cape region — which genus?
Gladiolus: Genus of perennial flowering plants. It is sometimes called the 'sword lily', but is usually called by its generic name (plural gladioli).

Once classified as a subfamily of the seabasses, this diverse family of marine ray-finned fish is now treated as distinct, with most members drawn from two large genera. What are they commonly called?
Grouper: Family of fishes. The common name "grouper" is usually given to fish in one of two large genera: Epinephelus and Mycteroperca.
About the size of a closed fist and enclosed in a protective sac called the pericardium, this four-chambered organ sits in the chest between the lungs and pumps blood through the body — which organ?
Heart: Organ found in humans and other animals.
This genus of over 570 flowering plants — the only living genus in its family — includes the evergreen shrub famous for Christmas decorations and cards. What genus is it?
Holly: Genus of flowering plants. Ilex or holly is a genus of over 570 species of flowering plants in the family Aquifoliaceae, and the only living genus in that family.

This neurological disorder involves excessive sleepiness or time spent sleeping, sometimes linked to seasonal affective disorder, and appears under sleep-wake disorders in the DSM-5 — what is it called?

Hypersomnia: Neurological disorder of excessive time spent sleeping or excessive sleepiness. It can have many possible causes (such as seasonal affective disorder) and can cause distress and problems with functioning.
More than half of all animal species belong to this one chitinous-shelled group, each member sporting three body parts and three pairs of jointed legs — who are they?
Known as the 'snow monkey' for surviving areas buried in snow half the year, no other primate lives farther north than this species — which one?
Japanese macaque: Species of Old World monkey.
A 1983 MacArthur Fellow, this American mathematician's work on Hilbert's tenth problem proved crucial to its eventual resolution — now known as the MRDP theorem. Who was she?

Derived from a Greek word meaning 'hump,' this abnormal, excessive curving of the upper spine can result from osteoporosis, disc disease, or a condition common in teens called Scheuermann's disease — what is it called?
Kyphosis: Excessive convex curvature of the lower and middle spine.
Used to treat everything from pneumonia to Legionnaires' disease, this broad-spectrum fluoroquinolone antibiotic is the left-handed mirror-image isomer of a drug called ofloxacin — what is it?
Levofloxacin: Antibiotic. Levofloxacin, sold under the brand name Levaquin among others, is a broad-spectrum antibiotic of the fluoroquinolone drug class.
Sometimes called the Japanese medlar or Japanese plum, this evergreen tree from the hills of south-central China produces small orange fruit — which plant?
Loquat: Species of plant. The loquat (Eriobotrya japonica, Chinese: 枇杷; Pinyin: pípá) is a large evergreen shrub or tree grown commercially for its orange coloured fruits.
This category of health conditions arises from too few, too many, or an imbalance of nutrients, and can cause anything from stunted growth to obesity. What is it called?
Malnutrition: Medical condition caused by receiving too little or too many nutrients.

Selected in 1969 as a dedicated air-superiority fighter and first flown in 1972, this twin-engine American jet boasts a staggering combat record of 106 victories and zero losses — which aircraft is it?
McDonnell Douglas F-15 Eagle: Multirole and air superiority fighter family.

Born from the French Revolution's push to standardize units into the metric system, this scientific field oversees everything from the SI unit system to the labs that keep rulers honest — what is it called?
Metrology: Science of measurement and its application.
With shovel-like front limbs built for burrowing and a mating song broadcast from a specially shaped underground tunnel, which insect is this?
Mole cricket: Members of the insect family Gryllotalpidae.
This symbiotic partnership between fungus and plant roots plays a crucial role in plant nutrition and soil chemistry — usually mutualistic, but sometimes parasitic. What's the association called?
Mycorrhiza: Fungus-plant symbiotic association. The term mycorrhiza refers to the role of the fungus in the plant's rhizosphere, the plant root system and its surroundings.

Published in the Principia Mathematica, this principle holds that every particle in the cosmos attracts every other with a pull proportional to their masses and inversely proportional to the squared distance between them — which principle is it?
Newton's law of universal gravitation: Classical statement of gravity as force.

This family within the superfamily Delphinoidea includes species with 'whale' in their common names, like the pilot and false killer types, and ranges up in size to the massive orca — what is this family called?
Oceanic dolphin: Family of marine mammals.

Triggered by a surge of luteinizing hormone near the midpoint of the menstrual cycle, this event sees the ovarian follicle rupture and release an egg — which breaks down in under a day if it isn't fertilized. What is it called?
Ovulation: Release of egg cells from the ovaries.
This economist and longtime New York Times columnist was the sole winner of the 2008 Nobel for his work on new trade theory and economic geography. Who is he?
Sold under brand names like Sudafed PE, this nasal decongestant works as a selective alpha-1 adrenergic receptor agonist — what is the drug?
Phenylephrine: Decongestant medication. It is unclear whether its use during pregnancy and breastfeeding is safe.
This egg-laying Australian mammal hunts with its eyes, ears, and nostrils shut, sensing prey by electrolocation — and, oddly for a mammal, it's also venomous. What is it?
Platypus: Species of mammal. Like other monotremes, the platypus has a sense of electrolocation, which it uses to detect prey in water while its eyes, ears and nostrils are closed.
This legal document spells out how a business collects, stores, and shares personal details like your address, financial records, or medical history — what is it called?
Privacy policy: Management of personal data across media.
Recognizable by its bold red-and-black pattern, this true bug is often confused with the unrelated cinnamon bug and forms large aggregations across Europe and Asia — which species is it?
Pyrrhocoris apterus: Species of true bug. The firebug, Pyrrhocoris apterus, is a common insect of the family Pyrrhocoridae.
Scholars call it an "essentially contested concept" with no agreed definition, but it broadly links humanity to the supernatural through behaviors, ethics, texts and sacred places — what is it?
This enormous flowering-plant family, named for its type genus, gives us apples, cherries, strawberries, and ornamental roses alike — which plant family is it?
Rosaceae: Rose family of flowering plants.
A former finance minister and central bank board member, this economist became the 52nd president of Paraguay in 2023 after switching from a liberal party to the Colorado Party — who is he?
Santiago Peña: President of Paraguay since 2023. Peña served on leadership boards for the Central Bank of Paraguay and Banco Amambay.
Considered paradoxical by the ancient Greeks in Zeno's puzzle about motion, what term describes an infinite sum of terms added one after another, later made rigorous through the concept of a limit?
Series (mathematics): Infinite sum. In mathematics, a series is, roughly speaking, an addition of infinitely many terms, one after the other.
The sixth most abundant element in Earth's crust, this soft alkali metal carries symbol Na and pairs with chlorine as the ocean's most common dissolved element — what is it?
Sodium: Chemical element with atomic number 11 (Na)
This Polish-American mathematician on the Manhattan Project dreamed up the cellular automaton and the Monte Carlo method, and co-designed the thermonuclear bomb — who was he?
Stanisław Ulam: Polish mathematician and physicist (1909–1984)
This medical specialty uses manual and instrumental techniques to treat disease, reshape the body, or remove diseased tissue, performed by a lead practitioner and an assistant?
Surgery: Medical procedures that involve incisive or invasive instruments into body cavities.
This cloud-based messaging service, known for large group chats and channels, launched on iOS in August of which year?
Telegram launched for iOS on 14 August 2013 and for Android on 20 October 2013, allowing users to exchange messages, share files and hold voice or video calls.
This blood-feeding arachnid's oldest fossils date back roughly 100 million years to the Cretaceous, and it comes in two main flavors: hard-bodied and soft-bodied — which parasite?
Tick: Order of arachnids in the arthropod phylum.

This genetic disorder causes small body size, heart defects, clenched fists with overlapping fingers, and severe intellectual disability, with risk rising alongside maternal age. What's the condition?
Trisomy 18: Chromosomal disorder in which there are three copies of chromosome 18.
Native to Europe and southwestern Asia, this herbaceous perennial is the type species that lends its name to an entire genus of flowering plants — what is it?
Valerian (herb): Species of flowering plant. Valerian (Valeriana officinalis) is an herbaceous perennial flowering plant in the family Caprifoliaceae, native to Europe and southwestern Asia.
Denoted by the Greek letter lambda, this measure of a repeating wave's spatial period shrinks as frequency rises for a wave moving at constant speed — what is it called?
Wavelength: Distance over which a wave's shape repeats.
Native to South America and first cultivated by the Guaraní people, the steeped leaves of this holly-genus plant produce a caffeinated beverage — what is it?
Yerba mate: South American holly plant. Yerba mate or yerba maté ( YUR-bə MAH-tay), Ilex paraguariensis, is a plant species of the holly genus native to South America.
The symbol for tungsten is W. Tungsten is a chemical element; it has symbol W and atomic number 74.
The symbol for platinum is Pt. Platinum is a chemical element; it has symbol Pt and atomic number 78.
